info.title: HEVN Platform API
info.description: HEVN's account, verification and money-movement API. Verification follows a submission workflow: save applicant info and documents, inspect outstanding requirements, then explicitly complete the submission to send an immutable snapshot for review. Completing a submission is separate from editing it.

post.summary: Start a developer-key login and receive the payload to sign
post.description: Starts a developer-key login. Sign the decoded `payload` and exchange it once at `POST /dapi/v1/auth/token` before `expiresAt`. Any problem with the email, the key, its allowlist, the signer or the signature returns `401 invalid_credentials` without naming the check.

post.summary: Exchange a signed login challenge for a session
post.description: Exchanges a signed challenge for an access token and a refresh token. A used challenge returns `409 challenge_consumed` and an expired one `410 challenge_expired`. The body of `POST /dapi/v1/auth/challenge` is also accepted for a one-call login. Where that form is not enabled, the call returns `501 login_mode_unavailable` and `details.use` names the challenge route.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a session, optionally acting for an account
post.description: Send the refresh token as the bearer, with an empty body or a `userId`. Returns a new access token and no new refresh token. A deleted key or a source address outside the key's allowlist returns `403 forbidden`.

post.summary: Create a client
post.description: Open a company account for a client of yours. HEVN keeps no wallet for it, so register the client's addresses through `/client/accounts`. Returns 202 with the client in `provisioning`. Poll `pollUrl` with the returned id in `X-Hevn-Account` until it is `ready`, which it becomes once the account exists and holds an active external account. Retrying with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the same client.

get.description: Every active external account and sub account of the client selected by `X-Hevn-Account`, oldest first; `kind` tells them apart. An external account is an address the client holds on one of the supported networks; it holds USDC only, and HEVN keeps no transaction history for it beyond the transfers HEVN itself arranges. post.summary: Add an account
post.description:
Without `kind`, or with `kind: external`: register an address for the client on `chain` (base, arb, eth, op, pol or sol). A receiving account opened on it delivers USDC on that network, an on-chain pay-in can be delivered to it, and a Base address can fund payouts it sends itself. Answers 201 the first time and 200 with `Idempotency-Replayed: true` when the same address was already added with the same label; another label is `account_address_taken`.

With `kind: sub`: open a sub account, a further wallet of your own account on Base that holds one token, `asset`: `USDC` (the default) or `RD`. The token is chosen once; receiving accounts, payouts and moves of the account run in it, and money moves only between accounts of the same token. Its address takes deposits at once; another token sent to it is not in `balance` and can only be moved out to the account's wallet with a swap. Name it as `sourceAccount` or `destinationAccount` on payouts, pay-ins and swaps, and as `accountId` on a receiving account; a payout or swap that leaves it is signed with your developer key, exactly like one that leaves the account's wallet. A create whose `label` and `asset` a sub account already carries answers 200 with that account; the same `label` with another `asset`, or a create without `label`, opens a new one. A sub account is opened on your own account only: a request that acts for a client returns `403 account_not_controlled`. An account whose wallet is not protected by co-signing returns `409 safe_mode_required`. A sub account cannot be archived.

put.description: Save information for the business applicant and its related individual applicants. The write updates an editable submission and starts no review. Send `company`, `people` and `documents` in one body or in separate calls, and a section you omit is unchanged. An unknown company enum value returns `422 invalid_enum_value` with `details.field` and `details.allowed`, and nothing is written. `ready: false` is a successful write, and `missing` names every outstanding field or document.

post.summary: Complete the verification submission
post.description: Send an immutable snapshot of the submission for compliance review. This is the only operation that starts review, and it takes no body. A new application returns `201` with `Location`. When the submission matches a pending or approved application, the call returns `200` with `Idempotency-Replayed: true` and that application. While `missing` has entries it returns `422 kyb_incomplete` with the same paths in `details.missing`. A file still being read returns `409 kyb_documents_processing`. Completing a changed submission supersedes a pending application, unless the call sends `Idempotency-Key`, which then returns `409 idempotency_key_reused`.

post.summary: Open an escrow and return the payer's approval
post.description: Create an escrow draft and return the payer's approval that funds it. The payer signs it on its own wallet: a developer key cannot, and a payer that owns its wallet is refused with `account_not_controlled` until it can approve in the HEVN sign-in window. No on-chain action is submitted until it is signed. Returns 201 with a `Location` header. A repeat with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns 200 with the same deal and windows. A different body under that key returns 409 `idempotency_key_reused` with `details.escrowId`. A zero duration returns 422 `validation_failed`.

post.summary: Create an outgoing transfer
post.description: Validate the contact, fix the payout terms and return how to authorize them. Returns `201` with `Location`. A retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` and terms returns `200`, `Idempotency-Replayed: true` and the same payout. The same key with another contact, `bankId`, pinned amount or `acc_` source returns `409 idempotency_key_reused` with `details.payoutId`. A `400` or `422` comes before booking, so the key stays usable for the corrected request. The `acc_` id of an external account as `sourceAccount` returns `authorization: wallet` with `transfer`, the USDC transfer that account sends itself, and has no confirm call. The `acc_` id of a sub account pays from that sub account and is authorized like a payout from the client's wallet: `authorization: debit`, with `debit` to sign and confirm with your developer key.

post.summary: Create a transfer between the client's own accounts
post.description: Price the swap, reserve it and return `201` with a `Location` header and the approval to sign. `authorization` says what the approval covers: a `debit` of the wallet that funds the swap, or an `intent` that settles against the signature. The same `Idempotency-Key` and body return the same swap with `200` and `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. The same key with a different body returns `409 idempotency_key_reused`. A session acting for a client through `X-Hevn-Account` gets `403 account_not_controlled`. The sandbox returns `422 swap_route_unavailable` for a swap between two wallet accounts and serves a move that names a sub account. The `acc_` id of a sub account on either side moves the token that sub account holds (USDC or RD) between the client's wallet and that sub account, or between two sub accounts of the same token, one for one, with `authorization: debit` of the account the money leaves. A sub account as `sourceAccount` with a wallet account of another token (`USDC`, `EURC` or `RD`) as `destinationAccount` moves that other token, sent to the sub account address by mistake, out to the wallet, one for one.

sourceAccount.title: Sourceaccount
sourceAccount.description: Account the money leaves. It must differ from `destinationAccount`. An `FDIC_*` account the owner does not hold returns `422 account_unavailable`. An `acc_` id names a sub account: the token it holds (USDC or RD) moves only to the wallet account of the same token (`USDC` or `RD`) or to another sub account of that token, one for one and without a fee. With a wallet account of another token (`USDC`, `EURC` or `RD`) as `destinationAccount`, the swap moves that other token, which the sub account does not hold but may have been sent, from the sub account address to the wallet, one for one and without a fee; nothing is converted. Anything else returns `409 source_account_unsupported`. The `acc_` id of an external account returns `404 account_not_found`.

destinationAccount.title: Destinationaccount
destinationAccount.description: Account the money lands on. An `FDIC_*` account the owner does not hold returns `422 account_unavailable`. An `acc_` id names a sub account: it takes the token it holds (USDC or RD) only from the wallet account of the same token or from another sub account of that token, and anything else, a move across tokens included, returns `409 account_destination_unsupported`.
